headline: EU Advances Plan for Two-Euro Customs Charge on E-Commerce Parcels
summary: The European Union is advancing a new two-euro customs administration fee on low-value e-commerce package imports to finance product safety checks and customs oversight, raising concerns among consumers and digital retailers.
why: Massive volumes of low-value cross-border e-commerce parcels entering the EU from Asian marketplaces have created regulatory and customs inspection challenges.

impacts.name: European E-Commerce
impacts.why: A flat two-euro customs levy increases end costs for cross-border e-commerce parcels and adds administrative friction.
